condition: Euglycaemic DKA on an SGLT2 inhibitor mimicking gastroenteritis
permutationLabel: Diabetic on SGLT2 inhibitor, euglycaemic DKA mimic
summary: 56-year-old man with type 2 diabetes on empagliflozin: 2 days of vomiting and abdominal pain labelled gastroenteritis; glucose 11.8, RR 28, HR 116, ketones 5.2, pH 7.12, bicarbonate 9. JBDS 2023/MHRA: check ketones regardless of glucose.

inputs.hpi: GP thinks gastroenteritis. Two days of vomiting, generalised abdominal pain and feeling breathless; hardly eating. Type 2 diabetes on empagliflozin and metformin; still taking both. Referred with a query of gallstones. No diarrhoea.

exam.general: Dry, deep sighing respirations, ketotic breath.
exam.abdomen: Soft, mild diffuse tenderness, no guarding, no peritonism.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Euglycaemic diabetic ketoacidosis (SGLT2 inhibitor)
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Euglycaemic DKA on empagliflozin (glucose 11.8, ketones 5.2, pH 7.12, bicarbonate 9): stop the SGLT2 inhibitor, fixed-rate insulin with glucose, fluids, emergency transfer.

mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: Web run 2026-09-25: not in top 3 of web.pane: 1. Acute Appendicitis | 2. Acute Cholecystitis | 3. Inguinal / Femoral Hernia. PANE has no DKA node; the web symptom inference has one (dka_hhs) but it did not rank.
mustNotMiss.proposedFix: Add a ketone check to the vomiting/abdominal-pain + diabetes cascade: any patient on an SGLT2 inhibitor (empagliflozin, dapagliflozin, canagliflozin, ertugliflozin) with vomiting, abdominal pain or Kussmaul breathing -> blood ketones and venous gas regardless of glucose (JBDS 2023, MHRA 2020).

mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: Web run 2026-09-25: not in top 5 of web.symptomInference: 1. Acute appendicitis (paediatric) | 2. Gallstone pancreatitis | 3. Acute cholecystitis | 4. Acute alcoholic pancreatitis | 5. Acute appendicitis.
mustNotMiss.proposedFix: symptom-inference dka_hhs: weight vomiting + abdominal pain + breathlessness in a known diabetic, and read SGLT2-inhibitor medication.

mustInclude.note: JBDS: fixed-rate IV insulin (with glucose once below 14 mmol/L) for DKA; a variable-rate regimen is the wrong protocol.

mustExclude.note: Wrong procedure: medical cause of abdominal pain.

mustExclude.knownGapNote: Web run 2026-09-25: forbidden management item present in web.managementPanel: "[surgical] laparoscopic appendicectomy (gold standard; reduces wound infection and los)." (+3 more).
mustExclude.proposedFix: Assessment panel follows the PANE top (appendicitis 0.261) instead of the confirmed E11.10; "no guarding, no peritonism" fires the generalised-peritonism prompt (negation). Prefer the locked working diagnosis and a negation-aware exam matcher.

guideline.name: JBDS-IP - The management of diabetic ketoacidosis in adults
guideline.section: DKA = ketonaemia >=3.0 mmol/L (or ketonuria 2+), blood glucose >11.0 mmol/L or known diabetes, and bicarbonate <15.0 mmol/L and/or venous pH <7.3; euglycaemic DKA occurs with SGLT2 inhibitors - glucose may be near normal; fixed-rate IV insulin with glucose-containing fluid
guideline.citation: Joint British Diabetes Societies for Inpatient Care. The management of diabetic ketoacidosis in adults (JBDS 02). 2023 update.

guideline.name: MHRA Drug Safety Update - SGLT2 inhibitors: risk of diabetic ketoacidosis
guideline.section: Measure ketones in patients on SGLT2 inhibitors with symptoms of DKA (nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain) even if glucose is near normal; interrupt treatment in acute illness
guideline.citation: Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency. Drug Safety Update, March 2020 (update of April 2016 advice).

rationale: Diabetic permutation and dangerous mimic: SGLT2-inhibitor euglycaemic DKA looks like gastroenteritis, and glucose-keyed rules (the web hyperglycaemia cascade needs >15 mmol/L) stay silent.
